concept.name: Container Image Scanning

relationships.description: Connects Container Image Scanning to canary deployments in the broader engineering catalog.

spark.summary: Static and runtime inspection of OCI container layers, OS packages, language lockfiles, and SBOMs to catch known CVEs, hardcoded secrets, and misconfigurations before pods ever schedule.
spark.keyTakeaway: Pair build-time SBOM generation (Syft/Trivy) with VEX-filtered admission gates (Kyverno/Cosign) so you block reachable critical CVEs without drowning engineers in unexploitable base-image noise.

concept.whyItMatters: A single container image bundles an entire Linux userland, language runtime, and dozens of transitive libraries. Vulnerabilities like CVE-2024-21626 (runc) or CVE-2021-44228 (Log4Shell) sit dormant in base layers until an attacker pivots from an exposed HTTP endpoint to host escape.
whenToUse: Every CI/CD build producing OCI images destined for staging or production Kubernetes clusters.
Admission control in Kubernetes (Kyverno or OPA Gatekeeper) to reject unsigned or unpatched images before pod scheduling.
Continuous registry re-scanning of already-deployed image digests when new CVEs publish to NVD, OSV, or distro security feeds.
whenNotToUse: As a substitute for runtime intrusion detection (eBPF sensors like Falco or Tetragon) against zero-day exploits.
To block PR merges on unfixed `LOW` or `MEDIUM` OS-package CVEs that have no upstream patch and no reachable code path.
On ephemeral local dev containers where blocking on network-fetched vulnerability DBs stalls developer iteration.
keyPoints: OCI images are stacked tarballs; a vulnerability deleted in a later `RUN rm` layer still exists in earlier layer blobs and remains extractable.

Distro-specific feeds (Alpine secdb, Debian Security Tracker, Red Hat OVAL) are far more accurate than raw NVD CPE matching because maintainers backport fixes without bumping upstream version numbers.
Generating a CycloneDX 1.5 or SPDX 2.3 SBOM once at build time lets you re-evaluate zero-day exposure in milliseconds without re-pulling multi-gigabyte images.
Cryptographic attestation via Sigstore Cosign binds the scan result and SBOM to the immutable `sha256` image digest, preventing tag-mutation bypasses.
VEX (Vulnerability Exploitability eXchange) documents and reachability analysis cut alert fatigue by 70–90% by suppressing CVEs in unused binaries or uncalled functions.

examples.title: Distroless Migration & CI Gate in Payments API
examples.scenario: A Go 1.22 payments microservice built on `ubuntu:22.04` (185 MB) triggered 47 `HIGH`/`CRITICAL` Trivy alerts per build—mostly in `openssl`, `curl`, and `apt`—causing developers to bypass the CI gate.
examples.outcome: Switching to `gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12` (2.4 MB) plus `govulncheck` call-graph reachability dropped total alerts to 2 actionable Go stdlib CVEs and cut image pull latency on autoscaled nodes from 14s to 1.2s.

examples.title: Zero-Day Triage via Registry SBOM Index
examples.scenario: When CVE-2024-3094 (`xz-utils` backdoor) broke, a platform team needed to identify affected workloads across 1,400 microservices running in 6 EKS clusters within 30 minutes.
examples.outcome: Instead of pulling 1.8 TB of layers from ECR, the security pipeline queried pre-generated CycloneDX SBOMs stored alongside image digests in Harbor, isolating the 11 affected build images in 45 seconds.

tradeOffs.pro: Failing CI on any `HIGH` or `CRITICAL` CVE prevents known-exploitable code from reaching production.
tradeOffs.con: Unfixed upstream OS CVEs can freeze all hotfixes unless paired with `--ignore-unfixed` or time-bound VEX exceptions.

tradeOffs.pro: Eliminating shells, package managers, and libc bloat removes 80%+ of the CVE surface area.
tradeOffs.con: Engineers cannot `kubectl exec` into a shell and must rely on `kubectl debug` ephemeral containers and structured telemetry.

tradeOffs.factor: Central Registry Scanning vs. CI-Only Scanning
tradeOffs.pro: Registry scanners catch newly disclosed CVEs against long-lived running images that haven't been rebuilt in weeks.
tradeOffs.con: Requires persistent storage, DB sync bandwidth, and automated Jira/Slack routing so stale findings actually get patched.

failureModes.name: Tag Mutation Bypass (TOCTOU)
failureModes.description: CI scans `myapp:v1.4.2`, passes, and pushes; an attacker or misconfigured pipeline overwrites the mutable tag before Kubernetes pulls it.
failureModes.mitigation: Sign immutable `sha256` digests with Cosign and enforce digest-only references in Kyverno admission policies.

failureModes.name: Stale Vulnerability Database
failureModes.description: Air-gapped or cached CI runners scan against a Trivy/Grype DB that is 14 days old, silently missing newly published critical CVEs.
failureModes.mitigation: Enforce a max DB age check (`--db-repository` mirror synced every 6 hours) and fail builds if DB metadata is older than 24 hours.

failureModes.name: False Negatives on Static/Vendored Binaries
failureModes.description: Scanners inspecting only `/var/lib/dpkg` or `apk` miss statically linked Go, Rust, or C++ binaries compiled without embedded build-info or SBOM metadata.
failureModes.mitigation: Enable language-specific analyzers (`go.mod`, `Cargo.lock`, `package-lock.json`) and compile with Go `-buildinfo` / Syft source cataloging.

failureModes.name: Alert Fatigue & Blanket Exceptions
failureModes.description: Teams faced with 300 unfixable `MEDIUM` CVEs add global `.trivyignore` wildcards, accidentally suppressing future critical alerts.
failureModes.mitigation: Gate only on `CRITICAL`/`HIGH` with `fixed` status, require expiration dates on VEX exceptions, and auto-reopen expired waivers.

commonMistakes: Scanning only the Dockerfile base image instead of the final multi-stage output image containing application dependencies.
Leaving `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` or `.npmrc` tokens in intermediate `ARG`/`ENV` layers without using BuildKit `--mount=type=secret`.
Ignoring distro backport metadata and panicking over upstream version strings reported by naive CPE scanners.
Treating a clean scan at deploy time as permanent—an image scanned 30 days ago may have 5 new `CRITICAL` CVEs today.
Deleting sensitive files in a subsequent `RUN rm` instruction instead of using multi-stage builds, leaving secrets intact in earlier OCI layer blobs.

sections.content:
## The idea

Container image scanning treats an OCI image not as an opaque binary, but as a verifiable manifest of filesystem layers, package databases, and language dependency graphs. An OCI image consists of a JSON manifest pointing to a config blob and an ordered stack of compressed tar layers. Scanners like **Trivy** and **Grype** unpack these layers virtually (without executing the container), extract package manifests (`/var/lib/dpkg/status`, `/lib/apk/db/installed`, `go.mod`, `package-lock.json`, `pom.xml`), and cross-reference exact package-version pairs against curated vulnerability advisories (NVD, OSV, GitHub Advisory Database, and vendor OVAL/secdb feeds).

Because modern supply-chain security separates *inventory* from *evaluation*, best-in-class pipelines first generate a standardized **SBOM** (CycloneDX 1.5 or SPDX 2.3) via **Syft** or Trivy, attach **VEX** exploitability statements, and cryptographically sign the bundle to the immutable `sha256` digest with **Sigstore Cosign**. Admission controllers then verify both the signature and policy compliance in milliseconds at cluster scheduling time.

## Concrete walkthrough

Consider a Python 3.12 FastAPI service built via GitHub Actions and deployed to Amazon EKS:

1. **Multi-stage build & secret hygiene**: Stage 1 installs `uv` dependencies; Stage 2 copies only the virtualenv into `cgr.io/chainguard/python:latest` (~48 MB) using BuildKit `--mount=type=secret` for private PyPI credentials.
2. **Inventory & Scan**: `trivy image --format cyclonedx --output sbom.cdx.json ghcr.io/acme/billing@sha256:9f8a...` catalogs 38 Wolfi APK packages and 64 Python wheels in ~4.2 seconds using a cached 45 MB BoltDB.
3. **Policy Evaluation**: A follow-up `trivy sbom --severity CRITICAL,HIGH --ignore-unfixed --exit-code 1 sbom.cdx.json` checks the SBOM against the latest advisory feed and applies a signed `.vex.json` suppressing `CVE-2023-45853` (present in an unused `zlib` CLI tool).
4. **Attestation**: `cosign attest --predicate sbom.cdx.json --type cyclonedx ghcr.io/acme/billing@sha256:9f8a...` stores the signed SBOM in the OCI registry via Rekor transparency logs.
5. **Admission & Runtime**: Kyverno checks the Cosign signature and scan attestation age (<24h) before allowing the Pod to schedule, while registry webhooks re-evaluate stored SBOMs every 6 hours.

sections.content:
## Layer mechanics, backports, and reachability

Naive vulnerability scanners match software names to NVD Common Platform Enumeration (CPE) strings, producing massive false-positive rates on Linux distributions. Debian, Ubuntu, RHEL, and Alpine routinely backport security patches into older upstream package versions (for example, `openssl 3.0.11-1~deb12u2` remains `3.0.11` upstream while containing the fix for a `3.0.13` CVE). Distro-aware scanners parse `/etc/os-release` and query vendor-specific security trackers first.

Beyond OS packages, application-level reachability separates theoretical exposure from real risk. Tools like `govulncheck` or Endor Labs construct call graphs from `main()` to third-party symbols: if your service imports `golang.org/x/net` solely for `html.EscapeString`, a CVE inside `http2.Server` is unreachable at runtime and can be documented via a VEX `code_not_in_execute_path` statement.

## Scanner & base image comparison

| Tool / Base | Primary Role | Advisory Sources | Typical Footprint / Speed | Key Strength |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Trivy** | All-in-one image, SBOM, IaC, secret scanner | NVD, OSV, Alpine, Debian, Red Hat, GitHub | ~45 MB DB; 3–8s per image | Single binary, built-in VEX & secret scanning |
| **Syft + Grype** | Decoupled SBOM generator + CVE matcher | Anchore feed, NVD, OSV, distro feeds | ~120 MB DB; 2–6s per image | Best-in-class deep artifact & Java/JAR cataloging |
| **Docker Scout** | Registry-integrated image & base advisor | Docker, NVD, vendor feeds | SaaS / CLI; <5s cached | Automated base-image upgrade PR suggestions |
| **Distroless (`debian12`)** | Minimal runtime base image | Debian Security Tracker | 2–25 MB; 0–3 CVEs | Zero shell, zero `apt`, minimal attack surface |
| **Chainguard Wolfi** | Undistro base with daily APK rebuilds | Wolfi SecDB + OSV | 15–50 MB; near-zero CVEs | Daily patched packages with native Cosign SBOMs |

## Failure modes

The most dangerous failure mode is **digestless deployment**: scanning `:latest` or `:v1.2` in CI and deploying by tag allows a stale or compromised image to slip past admission. A close second is **secret persistence across layers**—copying `.env` or SSH keys in layer 3 and deleting them in layer 4 leaves the secret readable via `docker save` or `skopeo copy`. Finally, **unbounded policy gates** that block builds on unfixed `MEDIUM` CVEs force engineers to add blanket `.trivyignore` waivers, eroding trust in the entire security pipeline.

## Runtime correlation and continuous triage

Static scanning cannot tell you whether a vulnerable shared library is actually loaded into process memory. Pairing build-time SBOMs with runtime eBPF telemetry (such as **Tetragon** or **Falco**) closes the loop: if a newly disclosed `CRITICAL` CVE hits an image running across 40 pods, runtime process/file-open telemetry identifies which pods actually execute the affected binary, letting SREs prioritize rolling restarts in minutes instead of orchestrating blind cluster-wide drains.

## Practical checklist

- Switch production stages to **Distroless**, **Chainguard Wolfi**, or `scratch` using multi-stage Dockerfiles.
- Use BuildKit `--mount=type=secret` for private package registries; run `trivy fs --scanners secret` on every PR.
- Generate a **CycloneDX 1.5** or **SPDX 2.3** SBOM during CI and push it as a Cosign-signed OCI attestation.
- Gate CI merges strictly on `CRITICAL` and `HIGH` CVEs with `--ignore-unfixed`, routing `MEDIUM`/unfixed items to an async backlog.
- Enforce `sha256` digest pinning and Cosign signature verification in **Kyverno** or **OPA Gatekeeper**.
- Schedule registry-side SBOM re-evaluation every 6 hours to detect zero-day drift on already-running workloads.

interviewProblems.title: Container Image Scanning
interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: Design a production system that depends on Container Image Scanning. What invariants, failure modes, and observability do you require?
interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Start from invariants, choose the pattern that preserves them, and add metrics for the known failure modes.
commonPitfalls: Optimizing throughput before defining correctness boundaries.

steps.title: 1. Normal Request Ingress
steps.explanation: Static and runtime inspection of OCI container layers, OS packages, language lockfiles, and SBOMs to catch known CVEs, hardcoded secrets, and misconfigurations before pods ever schedule.

steps.title: 2. Core Execution & State Lookup
steps.explanation: OCI Registry + Cosign applies the primary invariant and coordinates with Kyverno Admission Gate.

steps.title: 3. Scale Spike / Failure Injection
steps.explanation: Under a 10x burst, Kyverno Admission Gate experiences contention and tail-latency amplification.

steps.title: 4. Mitigation & Steady Recovery
steps.explanation: Sign immutable `sha256` digests with Cosign and enforce digest-only references in Kyverno admission policies.

tipsAndTricks: Core mental model: Pair build-time SBOM generation (Syft/Trivy) with VEX-filtered admission gates (Kyverno/Cosign) so you block reachable critical CVEs without drowning engineers in unexploitable base-image noise.
Avoid trap: Scanning only the Dockerfile base image instead of the final multi-stage output image containing application dependencies.
Avoid trap: Leaving `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` or `.npmrc` tokens in intermediate `ARG`/`ENV` layers without using BuildKit `--mount=type=secret`.
When to reach for it: Every CI/CD build producing OCI images destined for staging or production Kubernetes clusters.
When to reach for it: Admission control in Kubernetes (Kyverno or OPA Gatekeeper) to reject unsigned or unpatched images before pod scheduling.

putItTogether.title: Putting Container Image Scanning Together
putItTogether.summary: Pair build-time SBOM generation (Syft/Trivy) with VEX-filtered admission gates (Kyverno/Cosign) so you block reachable critical CVEs without drowning engineers in unexploitable base-image noise.
steps: Establish baseline invariants for Container Image Scanning before scaling.
Isolate hot paths with caching, backpressure, or partitioning.
Verify failure modes with synthetic load & chaos checks.
putItTogether.outcome: Switching to `gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12` (2.4 MB) plus `govulncheck` call-graph reachability dropped total alerts to 2 actionable Go stdlib CVEs and cut image pull latency on autoscaled nodes from 14s to 1.2s.
